svg.title: Three knobs on a stateful checkpoint
svg.desc: A stateful checkpoint stores one RocksDB instance per partition, and each key hashes to one of them. Changing spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is ignored. State rebalancing keeps the same count and moves instances onto new executors. spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.partitions restarts the query, finishes the pending microbatch, and runs one control batch that rehashes state into a new count.

g.text: The checkpoint is the layout
One RocksDB instance per partition. A key hashes to one instance.
The count was written when the checkpoint was created. A later shuffle.partitions value is not read.
RocksDB is required. The provider cannot be swapped without a new checkpoint.
Ignored change
Set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions.
Restart. The old count still runs.
The lock is there so a new hash
cannot point at an empty instance
while the bytes sit in the old one.
The October stateful-streaming page
still prints this as the rule, then
carves out Runtime 18 underneath it.
A new checkpoint location is the
old way to apply a new count.
That path drops the state.
Stateless queries are not this box.
Their shuffle count can change
without a new checkpoint.
They have no RocksDB layout to move.
Same count, new executors
State rebalancing.
A cluster resize moves instances.
The partition count stays.
State loads from cloud storage
onto the new executors.
Micro-batches can slow while it loads.
On for Lakeflow streaming by default.
Elsewhere, from Runtime 11.3 LTS,
the stateRebalancing config.
This does not fix a count of 200
that no longer matches the cores.
The sizing note is still 1 to 2 times
the cores. Rebalancing does not
rewrite that number.
A hot key still hashes to one instance.
New count, same checkpoint
spark.sql.streaming.
stateStore.partitions.
It wins over shuffle.partitions.
Stop. Set. Start the same path.
Finish the last planned microbatch.
Then one repartition batch.
durationMs controlBatch.REPARTITION
is the duration, after the next batch.
A failed or abandoned batch blocks
the next count. Retry that batch.
RocksDB. Runtime 18.
Lakeflow sets the same key on
the table or append_flow decorator.
Not a live resize. A maintenance pause.
What I would write next to the diagram
13 October release notes: generally available. 14 September post and the 10 June runtime bullet: Public Preview.
Runtime 18 is Spark 4.1.0. Spark 4.1 has the stateless shuffle change. The Spark 4.2 runner is not user-facing.
A hot key is still one partition after the rehash. More partitions share the same per-node RocksDB memory cap.
The TransformWithState method in the runtime notes is not on the feature page. I would not call it from a runbook.
An abandoned repartition has to be retried at the same count before a different count is legal.
